sections.title: Tree and leaves
sections.text: Streblus asper, the sandpaper tree, is an evergreen Asian tree reaching about 10 m. Its stiff, alternate leaves are elliptic, roughly 2.5–6 × 2–3.5 cm, with a leathery, conspicuously rough surface.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Tiny flowers form dense heads; male and female flowers are usually separate, and the small yellow drupes are about 6 mm across. The plate depicts the coarse foliage, clustered flowers and fruiting structure.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: Regional botanical references report the ripe fruit as edible. The species also has traditional material uses, but medicinal claims are outside this description.
